_readme: Load forecasts and data-center pipelines. Each record: entity, metric, value, unit, as_of, source, url, verified, notes. verified=true means the number was read in the cited document this session; false means it came only from a search-result summary or secondary coverage. 'Pipeline' numbers are requests/prospects, not commitments, and definitions differ by utility.

national_estimates.source: LBNL 2024 United States Data Center Energy Usage Report (Shehabi et al.)
national_estimates.notes: Verified via DOE release summary; LBL PDFs return HTTP 403 to scripts.
The 6.7-12.0% range is restated in the LBNL 2025 Update.

national_estimates.source: LBNL United States Data Center Energy Usage Report: 2025 Update (Smith, Hubbard, Newkirk ... Shehabi)
national_estimates.notes: 2024 is the last historical year; lands at the low end of the 2024 report's range.
Data centers would be ~33% of total US load growth 2024-2030 (using NERC 2025 LTRA totals).

rto_forecasts.notes: 2026 peak (Jul 2) is the highest since at least 2009; 2014-2024 summer peaks averaged 144,493 MW and never exceeded 150,000 MW.

rto_forecasts.source: IMM 2028/29 BRA Part A, Table 4 (from PJM load forecast reports)
rto_forecasts.notes: PJM attributes almost all of the upward revisions to data centers.
In the 2025 forecast, data centers were 93% (2026) and 95% (2027) of large-load adjustments.
2028/29 total of 21,470 MW = 5,034 MW existing + 16,436 MW forecast growth.

Near-term forecast cut because PJM now requires firm commitments (ESA/construction) for near-term large-load adjustments and derates non-firm projects. Zones adjusted for data-center growth: AEP, ATSI, APS, BGE, COMED, DAYTON, DLCO, JCPL, METED, PECO, PEPCO, PL, DOM, PS.

rto_forecasts.source: PJM Long-Term Load Forecast Report, January 2025
Maryland OPC FERC complaint (citing PJM materials)
rto_forecasts.notes: Secondary citation of PJM figures inside a primary legal filing.

rto_forecasts.source: ERCOT, Texas Senate panel 'Assessing the Grid', July 29, 2026
rto_forecasts.notes: ~205 GW eligible for 'Batch Zero' studies based on existing studies (data as of 2026-07-28); 315 projects had no qualifying study. ERCOT 2025 summer peak is far below these numbers (requests, not forecasts).

rto_forecasts.source: ERCOT board updates via Utility Dive / Latitude Media; Senate deck
rto_forecasts.notes: Only the 474 GW value was read in the ERCOT PDF; earlier points from search summaries. Texas SB 6 (2025) sets large-load interconnection standards and curtailment rules.

rto_forecasts.notes: Search-summary only; MISO describes large-load additions as preliminary.

rto_forecasts.notes: Thin/secondary; check SPP 2026 ITP load forecast.

utility_pipelines.notes: Context (verified in MD OPC complaint citing Dominion IRP): 3.6 GW of data-center demand in the Dominion zone in Dec 2024 (+660% MWh since 2013); ~40 GW of capacity requests in 2024 alone; Dominion peak 24,271 MW (2025) -> 31,939 MW (2030); 88 data-center-driven transmission projects ($2.44bn).

utility_pipelines.contracted_definition: signed large-load contracts (Georgia Power share of Southern's 21 GW)
utility_pipelines.total_pipeline_definition: Southern Co. 'prospective pipeline' to be risk-adjusted
utility_pipelines.source: Southern Co. Q3 2026 earnings via GuruFocus, Georgia PIRG
utility_pipelines.notes: Georgia Power-only pipeline reported at ~50.9 GW in one Utility Dive piece (date unclear). Georgia PSC approved a base-rate freeze through 2028 and a ~$50/yr rate cut credited to large-load revenue (EEI).

utility_pipelines.notes: Q2 2026: 69 GW through 2030, of which Texas 45 GW. AEP $100bn 2027-2031 capital plan. AEP Ohio data-center tariff approved 2025 (minimum-demand payment of 85% of contracted capacity: UNVERIFIED, from memory).

utility_pipelines.contracted_definition: signed deals over prior year (Q4 2025 call)
utility_pipelines.source: Entergy earnings calls via Nasdaq/Motley Fool
utility_pipelines.notes: Includes Meta Hyperion (Richland Parish, ~5 GW site per atlas). Capital plan raised $14bn to $57bn largely for Meta.

utility_pipelines.source: Utility Dive / Texas House hearing slides
utility_pipelines.notes: April 2026 hearing: 650 requests totaling 273 GW. Harvard ELI (Mar 2025) cited 82 GW of potential DC load.

utility_pipelines.source: Xcel Q2 2026 earnings via Utility Dive / T&D World

PG&E expects to serve ~1.8 GW of new data-center demand by 2030; argues added load can lower rates by spreading fixed costs.
